recent_posts.title: How RAG for customer support improves accuracy at scale
recent_posts.summary: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) for customer support grounds AI responses in an external knowledge base rather than relying solely on training data, reducing hallucinations and improving accuracy. A RAG pipeline moves through five stages: ingestion, indexing, retrieval, augmentation, and generation. Key use cases include customer-facing chatbots, agent assist tools, semantic knowledge base search, and ticket summarization. The post also covers how to evaluate AI model selection criteria (LLM quality, integration, cost, security), when companies are ready to implement RAG (data maturity, ticket volume, technical capacity), and the difference between RAG and fine-tuning. Agentic RAG is introduced as a multi-step reasoning variant. Meilisearch's hybrid search is highlighted as a retrieval layer that reduces noise reaching the LLM.

recent_posts.title: AI-powered workplace search: how it works, benefits, and more
recent_posts.summary: AI-powered workplace search connects all company tools into a unified search interface that understands natural language and user intent. Unlike traditional keyword search, it uses NLP and semantic search (via embeddings) to surface relevant documents even when exact terms don't match. A practical implementation walkthrough using Meilisearch and the OpenAI embeddings API demonstrates indexing documents with vectors, configuring hybrid search (keyword + semantic), and enforcing role-based access control. Key benefits include eliminating knowledge silos, reducing duplicated work, and saving the ~20% of workweek employees waste searching for information.

recent_posts.title: Meilisearch Launch Week April 2026 recap: everything that shipped
recent_posts.summary: Meilisearch's April 2026 Launch Week shipped five major releases: self-serve sharding and replication for horizontal scaling and high availability on Cloud; enterprise SSO/SAML with SCIM lifecycle management plus MFA for all accounts; a point-and-click Chat UI in the Cloud dashboard for building RAG-powered chat experiences; a Search Performance Inspector that breaks down query latency by component; and two experimental features — Document Joins (cross-index filtering via a `_foreign` keyword) and Dynamic Search Rules for pinning specific documents at exact result positions based on query conditions.

recent_posts.title: Conversational search, out of the box: introducing Meilisearch Chat
recent_posts.summary: Meilisearch Cloud now includes a built-in chat UI that enables conversational search without building a custom RAG pipeline. When you select an index, it automatically samples your documents, generates a grounded system prompt, sets default guardrails, and creates a search description. An inspector tab shows every tool call and raw LLM message for debugging, and an integrate tab provides ready-to-use code snippets. Upcoming features include multi-index chat, more granular guardrail controls, and richer inspector tooling.

recent_posts.title: Scale without limits: introducing sharding & replication in Meilisearch Cloud
recent_posts.summary: Meilisearch Cloud now supports horizontal sharding and replication for enterprise search deployments. Sharding distributes large datasets across multiple nodes to handle data volumes beyond what a single instance can serve, while replication keeps identical copies across nodes for high read availability and geo-distribution. The two features are composable — teams can run sharding only, replication only, or both simultaneously (e.g., 5 shards × 2 replicas = 10 nodes). Currently available as an enterprise add-on configured by the Meilisearch team, with a self-serve UI and improved cluster observability on the roadmap.

recent_posts.title: RAG-as-a-Service: what it is, use cases, providers & more
recent_posts.summary: RAG-as-a-Service (RAGaaS) is a managed cloud solution that handles the full retrieval-augmented generation pipeline—document ingestion, chunking, embedding, retrieval, and LLM generation—without requiring teams to build their own ML infrastructure. Key benefits include faster time to market, reduced infrastructure overhead, built-in scalability, and enterprise features like source citations and access control. Common use cases include customer support chatbots, internal knowledge bases, product copilots, and compliance Q&A. The post covers how RAGaaS works end-to-end, what features to look for (hybrid search, reranking, metadata filtering, granular access control), challenges like cost unpredictability and data freshness lag, and how to evaluate providers such as Nuclia, Vectara, and Pinecone. Meilisearch is positioned as a retrieval layer component for teams building their own RAG systems.

recent_posts.title: How Touchless powers instant, scalable vehicle search for large dealer groups
recent_posts.summary: Touchless, a Toronto-based automotive tech company, uses Meilisearch to power vehicle inventory search for large dealer groups. Their marketplace platform serves dealer groups with 3,000–9,000 vehicles per group across ~100 locations. Key reasons for choosing Meilisearch over Algolia include API flexibility, seamless integration with their custom Cloudflare edge-based EXO rendering system, and cost efficiency. Each dealer group gets a dedicated index that spins up in ~100ms, enabling a full live preview in 20 minutes. The result is instant faceted filtering, infinite scroll, and a modern car-shopping experience that drives higher conversion rates.

recent_posts.title: Self-RAG explained: how self-reflective retrieval boosts AI outputs
recent_posts.summary: Self-RAG (self-reflective retrieval-augmented generation) extends standard RAG by adding iterative self-evaluation loops. Instead of a single fixed retrieval step, the model assesses its own outputs, checks factual grounding and citation quality, and re-triggers retrieval when needed. This reduces hallucinations and improves reliability for complex queries. The post covers how self-RAG works using reflection and critique tokens, compares it to standard RAG, agentic RAG, and modular RAG, outlines its benefits (higher accuracy, better complex query handling) and limitations (higher compute cost, latency, complexity), and provides implementation guidance using tools like LangChain, Hugging Face, and Meilisearch as the retrieval backbone.

recent_posts.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Leaky: jemalloc, bumpalo, and mimalloc in Meilisearch
recent_posts.summary: A deep investigation into a memory leak in Meilisearch that persisted for 1.5 years. The root cause was twofold: a bumpalo bump allocator misuse where std::Vec objects stored inside bumpalo::Vec never had their drop glue run, and a more significant issue where LMDB (a C library) and Meilisearch used different allocators (system allocator vs mimalloc v2), preventing memory page reuse. Switching to mimalloc v3 with its override feature to unify allocations across both Rust and C code resolved the leak, yielding lower RSS memory usage and performance improvements of around 13% in some benchmarks. The investigation used jemalloc's profiling tools and LLM-assisted heap analysis to identify the issues.

recent_posts.title: Meilisearch roadmap roundup: where we're heading
recent_posts.summary: Meilisearch's CEO outlines four major roadmap themes for 2026. First, scaling for any workload via distributed search (sharding/replication already in progress) and serverless indexes (Q3 2026) that move idle indexes to object storage, enabling affordable per-tenant isolation and a real free tier. Second, making hybrid search the default by simplifying embedding setup, building an AI gateway with caching and fallback, and training proprietary embedding/reranking models co-optimized with Meilisearch's keyword engine. Third, evolving from API to platform by surfacing all engine capabilities in the Cloud dashboard, adding observability tools like slow-query dashboards, telemetry alerts, and an AI diagnostic helper. Fourth, advancing RAG at scale through a smarter chat engine with parallel multi-search, dynamic facet discovery, conversational memory, and a multi-provider LLM gateway built in Rust supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, and others. All four themes are designed to compound, transforming Meilisearch into a complete information retrieval platform.
